page.layout: One column of text on a single printed page. Running head at top with page number 237 at right. Heading block (division number, title, subtitle) centred above the text. Salutation in italic, then body text in one column with a large initial E. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: XXXV. RESPONSORIA PRINCIPIS ANHALTINI AD Regem Navarræ.

p.i: Serenissime & Illustrissime Rex, Domine & consanguinee observantissime.

main_text.p: ETsi omnino confidimus Ser. vestram Reg. per legatum ad nos missum posse de omnibus, quæ hic acta fuerint fieri certiorem, tamen ut aliquid literarum etiam ad Ser. Reg. vestram daremus, & rerum gravitas, & Ser. vest. Reg. quæ apud nos plurimum valet, autoritas requirere visa fuit. Tantas enim res a tam Christiano Rege suscipi, quæ non solum ad gloriam Dei, salutem Reipub. Christianæ pacemq; publicam spectent, sed quæ etiam

page.notes: The initial E is a large decorative initial; read as "Etsi". The word "Christiano" is partly obscured by the italic setting; the reading "Christiano" is given as printed in the scan. Lines of the final paragraph run on to the page foot, where the word "etiam" appears set right, likely a catchword.
